Definition: from G5442; a guarding or (concretely, guard), the act, the person; figuratively, the place, the condition, or (specially), the time (as a division of day or night), literally or figuratively:--cage, hold, (im-)prison(-ment), ward, watch.
BiblicalUsage: Phylake is a guarding, a prison, a watch of the night — the place, the person, and the hour of keeping. Peter sleeps in prison while the church prays in Acts 12:5, and Paul and Silas sing in the inner prison in Acts 16:23. The same word is the shepherds keeping watch over their flock in Luke 2:8, and Jesus counts visiting the prisoner as visiting Him in Matthew 25:36.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe no prison wall shuts God out — He opens doors at night and turns a jail into a chapel. That is why I hold that the prisoner is never beyond His notice, and never beneath mine.
